findings.title: Interpolating before `querySupportsSplitting` breaks `$__range` detection
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on line 299 before passing the queries to `querySupportsSplitting(query)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries that use `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` (because splitting them causes the backend to re-evaluate the range against the 1-day chunk instead of the full query range). However, `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range*` in `query.expr` with the literal range duration (e.g., `7d`), so by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` runs, the variable reference is already gone and always evaluates to `false`. As a result, queries containing `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` will now be erroneously split into 1-day chunks, or `applyTemplateVariables` will have already baked in the unsplit range while `datasource.runQuery` may re-split the time range.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated multiple times when shard splitting delegates to `runSplitQuery`
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on all targets up front (line 52), and then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` delegates each shard batch to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which now also calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every target (as seen in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` line 112 where `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times for a single query). Because `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` also injects ad-hoc `request.filters` into the LogQL stream selector each time it is called, running `applyTemplateVariables` twice (and then a third time inside `super.query` / `runQuery`) will duplicate ad-hoc filter matchers in the query expression and can corrupt queries whose interpolated variable values contain `$` characters.
